title: Hired after a contract
question: Where a person appears to move between a department and an organization it funds, was there a new or enlarged contract between the two in the year before?
finding: Of the 8 name matches of a funded organization’s listed staff who then joined the department that funds it, 5 have a new or enlarged contract from that department to that organization dated in the year before or during the fiscal year they joined. In the other direction, of 11 former employees later listed at an organization their old department funds, 7 have such a contract between the year before they left and their first listing. Numbers this small show no pattern either way; organizations with standing yearly contracts will nearly always have one in any window.
how: The name matches are those already made in the site’s “People and roles” page (rare full names, with a second link, each labelled confirmed or not). This screen adds the dates: contract start dates and agreed amounts from the City’s contract table for that organization and that department, and Board-approved amendments, set against the fiscal year the person first appears on, or last appears on, the payroll (or the leaving date on their own Form 700 where there is one).
limits: The payroll file gives a fiscal year, not a start date, so “within a year” cannot be measured to the day. A name match is not a person: every row keeps the label the site’s “People and roles” page gave it. As the revolving-door screen in the site’s “People and roles” page states the City’s rule, a former employee may not for a year be paid by a contractor whose contract they personally helped award, and nothing here shows who took part in any award. Organizations funded every year have a contract in almost any window. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
